claim: Human burn wounds sustained during daylight hours were found to heal faster than those that occurred at night.

claim: In circadian entrained/rhythmic hamsters, cutaneous wounds created 3 hr after light onset healed faster than those created 2 hr after dark onset.
source: This observation is consistent with observations in circadian entrained/rhythmic hamsters in which cutaneous wounds created 3 hr after light onset healed faster than those created 2 hr after dark onset (Cable et al., 2017).

claim: Functional circadian rhythms exist in all cells and organs.

evidence: This is supported by a citation to Matsui et al., 2016.

claim: Circadian dysregulation is associated with a wide range of diseases.

claim: VAS values from the left- and right-side wounds remained comparable between sides.

claim: The peripheral zone of this model demonstrated secondary intention healing.

claim: The peripheral zone in the model is representative of dermal and subcutaneous wound healing and not the morpho-functional influences of deeper muscle layers.

source: Normal skin and hypertrophic scars both contain collagen fibers composed of type I and type III collagen molecules; however, hypertrophic scars exhibit irregular organization of collagen bundles (Cuttle et al., 2005).

source: Type III collagen is a homotrimer of alpha-1 chains and occupies the center of type I collagen fibrils (Keene et al., 1987).

claim: The increased FACIT type XIV collagen synthesis induced by exposure to Dwn1 may limit collagen fiber thickness and normalize dermal collagen fiber organization.
source: Knowing that a lack of type XIV collagen contributes to the abnormally thick type I collagen fibrils in skin in null mutation models (Ansorge et al., 2009), the increased FACIT type XIV collagen synthesis induced by exposure to Dwn1 may limit collagen fiber thickness and normalize dermal collagen fiber organization.

claim: The VAS time course profile of the Dwn1-treated group was significantly different from that of the vehicle control (two-way ANOVA: treatment p = 0.0075).

claim: The scar index of Dwn1-treated wounds was significantly lower than that of vehicle-treated wounds.

claim: Granulation tissue formation was downregulated by Dwn1 treatment.

claim: The vehicle control dermal wound showed significantly less tensile strength than that of intact skin on day 21 (t-test, p = 0.0048).

claim: The tensile strength in the vehicle control dermal wound (2.61 ± 0.91) was not significantly increased from that on day 14 (2.04 ± 0.48) (t-test, p = 0.1418).

evidence: This is supported by tensile strength testing data.

claim: This murine dorsal incisional wound model reaches healing 14 days postoperatively, after which recovery of mechanical properties equivalent to intact skin is not expected.
source: The tensile strength in the vehicle control dermal wound (2.61 ± 0.91) was not significantly increased from that on day 14 (2.04 ± 0.48) (t-test, p = 0.1418), suggesting that this murine dorsal incisional wound model reaches healing 14 days postoperatively, after which recovery of mechanical properties equivalent to intact skin is not expected.

claim: Dwn1 treatment virtually eliminated α-SMA-positive fibroblasts.

claim: Dwn1 prevents myofibroblast differentiation.
